title: Unit Supply Specialist (Unit Supply SPC)
raw_text:
10-92Y. MOS 92Y--Unit Supply Specialist (Unit Supply SPC), CMF 92 (Eff 202510)
    a. Major duties: The 92Y Unit Supply Specialist is responsible for managing and maintaining unit supplies and
equipment, including receiving, storing, and issuing supplies, maintaining accurate inventory records and
reporting discrepancies. They process requests, coordinate with logistics teams, and maintain unit supply records,
ensuring timely and efficient delivery of supplies and equipment. They provide customer service to unit personnel,
participate in unit deployments, prepare and load supplies and equipment for transport, playing a critical role in
ensuring units have the necessary resources to perform their missions effectively.
         (1) MOSC 92Y1O. Receive, inspect, and store organizational supplies and equipment, verifying quantities
and condition. Issue supplies to authorized personnel, maintaining accurate records of transactions. Organize and
maintain storage areas, ensuring accessibility and security. Perform basic ordering, inventory control, reporting
shortages or discrepancies using the automated supply system. Follow established procedures for handling and
disposing of waste materials. Assist with packing, crating, and shipping of supplies. Secures and controls weapon
parts, sensitive items in secure areas.
         (2) MOSC 92Y2O. Order and procure supplies using automated systems, ensuring timely delivery.
Manage and maintain stock levels, anticipating future needs and minimizing shortages. Schedule and conduct
periodic inventories, reconciling discrepancies and adjusting records. Prepare and process documentation for
supply transactions, maintaining accountability. Operate material handling equipment, safely moving supplies and
equipment. Assist with the preparation of reports on supply status and usage.
         (3) MOSC 92Y3O. Supervise supply operations, coordinating the flow of materials and equipment. Analyze
supply requirements, forecasting needs and optimizing stock levels. Manage and maintain automated supply
systems, ensuring data accuracy. Train and mentor junior supply personnel provide guidance and support.
Resolve supply discrepancies, investigating issues and implementing corrective actions. Prepare detailed reports
on supply status, usage, and expenditures. Assists and advises the supply officer and company commander.
         (4) MOSC 92Y4O. Manage all aspects of unit supply operations, including budgeting and resource
allocation. Develop and implement supply plans, aligning with operational requirements. Advise commanders on
supply matters, providing expert recommendations. Oversee the receipt, storage, issue, and disposal of all
supplies and equipment. Conduct comprehensive audits of supply accounts, ensuring accountability and
compliance. Coordinate with external agencies to procure specialized items and resolve complex supply issues.
Train and mentor junior supply personnel provide guidance and support.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Unit supply specialists must possess
the following qualifications:
         (1) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A physical profile of 222222.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) Qualifying scores.
             (a) A minimum score of 90 in aptitude area CL.
             (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350
cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand
Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
         (5) Mandatory formal training. Completion of MOS 92Y course conducted under the auspices of the U.S.
Army Quartermaster School; or meet the ACASP criteria listed in AR 601-210. Waiver requests can be submitted
to the Office of the Quartermaster Commandant Enlisted Proponent Office at USARMY Ft Lee VA, 23801.
TRADOC List QM Enlisted Personnel Development lee.tradoc.list.qm-enlisted-personnel-development@army.mil.
    c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-2 Listing of all ASIs).
         (1) D6--Operational Data Analyst (personnel only)
         (2) 3C--Operational Contract Support (OCS) (SSG and above).
    d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill level are
listed in the following tables:
         (1) Table 10-92Y-1. Physical requirements.
         (2) Table 10-92Y-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (3) Table 10-92Y-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
